attacks.claim: Zero-config discovery auto-loads any installed package (including transitive deps) with the `tasq-plugin` keyword and runs it before argument parsing, on every invocation including pre-commit hooks, CI and editors. There is no allowlist, opt-in or opt-out, so a compromised or typosquatted dependency gets code execution. The supply-chain section covers only tasq's own deps and postinstall, not this path.
attacks.evidence: "Any installed package with the `tasq-plugin` keyword is picked up automatically." and "Discovery runs before argument parsing so that plugins can register subcommands."

attacks.claim: The performance table shows roughly 10x regressions on the hot paths (`--version` 0.11s to 1.94s, cache-hit build 0.21s to 2.02s, lint-staged 0.38s to 2.31s). The prose says discovery is 'negligible' and that the 'under 50 ms' cache claim holds. Neither is supported by the table, and cost scales with installed package count. Discovery is a full glob of node_modules on every call, including pre-commit, with no discovery cache.
attacks.evidence: "Discovery is a fixed per-invocation cost and becomes negligible relative to real build work" vs "| `tasq run build` (cache hit) | 0.21 s | 2.02 s |"

attacks.claim: The discovery code has unhandled failure modes. A single malformed package.json aborts all discovery. `keywords` as a string would substring-match. Symlinks can escape the root. `dir` is relative while the read uses a joined path. The artifact defines no behavior when a plugin fails to load, so one broken plugin can break every command. Yarn PnP layouts (no node_modules) silently find nothing, and the artifact does not say what PnP users get.
attacks.evidence: const pkg = JSON.parse(await readFile(join(root, pkgJson), "utf8")); ... found.push({ name: pkg.name, dir: dirname(pkgJson) });

attacks.claim: The `plugins` array is silently ignored. Plugins that lack the keyword (local or private ones) stop loading with no warning, and `tasq-migrate` 'installs nothing new', so it does not flag them. Behavior changes silently for users with explicit plugin lists.
attacks.evidence: "`plugins` array in config ignored | Auto-discovery replaces it; `tasq-migrate` removes the array and installs nothing new"

attacks.claim: Rollback only re-points the `latest` dist-tag. It does not help users who pinned or locked 3.x, and users who already ran `tasq-migrate` have configs incompatible with 2.x. There is no reverse migration path or dry-run/backup for the migration tool.
attacks.evidence: "Rollback: if a P1 is found after promotion, re-point `latest` to `2.9.4`"
